# Huffel Peaks · Book II, pp. 236–241
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	236
P	This range runs along the western edge of the <b>Flats</b> (page 126) and the <b>Steplands</b> (page 372), connecting with the <b>Whitefang Mountains</b> (page 480) in the north.
P	They're not as tall and menacing as the Whitefangs, but they are jagged things of granite and basalt, home to a number of volcanoes, and rich in minerals and ore.
H2	Impressions
HR
H3	Always
B	Slabs of jagged stone: impassive, looming, somehow still surprising
B	Tall thin trees (aspen, pines, firs) in the lower slopes and valleys; windswept junipers higher up
B	The stone-on-stone clink and thunk as rocks tumble down a slope
B	A sense of being surrounded, cut off

PAGE	237
H2	The World's End
HR
P	Beyond the Huffel Peaks lies a vast expanse of water. But what lies between the mountains and the sea? That's for you and your group to decide, and the answer might vary depending on which direction you go through the mountains. But perhaps one might find...
E	mighty cliffs, pounded by relentless waves;
E	a gentle slope, a bountiful lowland, vast sandy beaches, a mild clime;
E	a chain of islands, some tiny, some quite large;
E	a wine-dark sea, the civilized lands of the south to be found at its farthest shores;
E	deserted ruins of the <b>Tempest Lords</b> (page 398), the <b>Forge Lords</b> (page 156) or both;
E	the <b>Ustrina</b> (page 464), in numbers far greater than anyone would suspect;
E	an isolated people, their ancestors a mix of refugees from when the <b>Makers</b> (page 264) fell;
E	colonies from the civilized lands of the <b>South</b> (page 256), eking out a living;
E	some combination of the above; or
E	something else entirely.
H2	Questions
HR
Q	Who did you once meet who claimed to have reached the far side of the Huffel Peaks? Do you believe their stories about an endless body of water?
Q	What legendary treasure is said to be hidden in those peaks?
Q	How long has it been since one of the volcanoes erupted violently? How did it affect Stonetop/Gordin's Delve/the Hillfolk?
Q	You don't really think that there are dragons in the Huffel Peaks, do you?

H2	Hooks
HR
B	Prospectors find veins of cinnabar near Gordin's Delve, and set about mining the lucrative, toxic stuff
B	A <b>draventao</b> (page 170) chases a <b>Hillfolk</b> (page 228) band from their winter camp in the mountains
B	Scouts and warbands of an unknown people start to appear in the Huffel Peaks
B	A massive volcanic eruption throws ash across the region, causes strange sunsets and weather, spreads panic and superstition, and perhaps sets loose a powerful <b>emanation</b> of the Things Below (page 436)

H3	Hazards
B	Getting lost (maze of mountains, canyons, passes, and valleys)
B	Sheer rock face to climb, and a reason to climb it

B	<b>Altitude sickness</b> (page 489), especially near the peaks
HR
H3	Harsh mountain weather
B	Baking sun, dry air, lack of water
B	Fog banks/low clouds, blocking vision and soaking everything
B	Buffeting wind, drowning out voices and keeping you off-balance
B	Powerful gusts, threatening to toss you aside
B	Rain and wind rolling up from below
B	Rain and sleet pelting you, soaking you, threatening to wash you away
B	Thunder or lightning: making you flinch/jerk/jolt, triggering rockslides
B	Brutal cold and ceaseless wind, leading to <b>hypothermia & frostbite</b> (page 489)
B	Snow and ice burying a pass or trail, making narrow paths impossible
B	Snow and ice building up, forming an <b>avalanche</b> (page 489)

H3	Earthquake
P	• The ground shakes briefly, alarming but not dangerous
P	• Powerful tremors make footing unstable, knock rocks loose, cause animals to panic
P	• Tremors persist: people lose their footing, large rocks tumble (d8 damage, <i>forceful</i>), trails and paths are damaged
P	• It's a big one: <b>mudslides</b> and <b>rockslides</b> (page 376), <b>avalanches</b> (page 489), whole rockfaces come tumbling down

ICON	icons/beast.svg
H3	Caralandrao
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>small</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>hoarder</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 3; <b>Armor</b> 2 (shell)
P	<b>Damage</b> pincers d4 with disadvantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> spider-climb, camouflaged shell
P	<b>Instinct</b> to feed on magic
P	• Sense mystic emanations from afar
P	• Get close without being noticed
P	• Skitter-skatter, dart and weave
P	• Make off with something magical
P	Are they crabs? Spiders? Hard to say.
P	Whatever they are, they've got too many too-long limbs, shells that blend in with the rocky terrain, and an appetite for magical artifacts. They'll drag their prizes back to their nests to feed. They can suck the power right out of minor trinkets, but powerful arcana can feed a small colony indefinitely.
P	And yet, they keep venturing out to find more.

ICON	icons/beast.svg
H3	Fire drake
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>aggressive</i>, <i>tough</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 10; <b>Armor</b> 2 (scales)
P	<b>Damage</b> bite d8 (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> fireproof; caustic, burning blood <b>Instinct</b> to get riled up easily
P	• Sound off in a deep, threatening chorus
P	• Blast a jet of burning, caustic blood from its eyes, d8 damage (<i>near</i>, <i>messy</i>, <i>reload</i>, ignores armor), but lose 1d4 HP
P	• Shake and worry and toss aside a foe it has bitten, d8+2 damage (<i>hand</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	Picture a horned lizard, but big as a large boar and with a mouth full of short jagged teeth. They're often encountered basking near hot springs or mudpots or other geothermal vents, soaking up the heat until they swell and glow like embers. Of course, once they notice you, they stop basking and start attacking.
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> Fire drake blood is caustic and catches fire when exposed to air; a jar of it deals d6 damage (<i>thrown</i>, <i>area</i>, <i>dangerous</i>, ignores armor, Value 1), but good luck harvesting it.
P	<b>Something useful:</b> The trick is to tap a vein with a metal tube, and drain the blood directly into a wax-sealed jar. Just… be careful.
HR
ICON	icons/beast.svg
H3	Frythanc fledgling
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>stealthy</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 6; <b>Armor</b> 0 (scales)
P	<b>Damage</b> talons d8+2 (hand, forceful), beak
P	d8 with disadvantage (hand)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> exceptional eyesight; terrible hearing
P	<b>Instinct</b> to eat and grow
P	• Cling to rock faces, camouflaged
P	• Strafe their prey
P	• Knock prey off a ledge
P	The full-grown frythancs that hunt the <b>Flats</b> (page 126) are terrors. Their young, thankfully, keep to the mountains. There, they hunt goats and sheep and the occasional unwary traveler. The fledglings aren't nearly as dangerous as their full-grown parents, but still, let's see how you do when birds with 12-foot wingspans try to tear you off some switchback trail.
